Time-optimal control policy for a hybrid electric race car
Mauro Salazar; Philipp Elbert; Søren Ebbesen; Carlo Bussi; Christopher H. Onder
IEEE Transactions on Control Systems Technology, 25(6), 1921–1934
Nov 2017
High — foundational F1 hybrid energy-management method
Derives a real-time energy-management policy using Pontryagin’s minimum principle and compares it with a global-optimum benchmark in simulation, including regulation-related constraints.

The work concerns a modeled hybrid race car and its internal controller, not reconstruction of hidden ERS state from public telemetry. Its powertrain assumptions reflect the earlier F1 hybrid architecture.
Use as the conceptual basis for treating energy state as a constrained dynamic process. Translate only the general control/constraint ideas; explicitly update assumptions for the 2026 regulations.

Time-optimal gearshift and energy management strategies for a hybrid electric race car
Pol Duhr; Grigorios Christodoulou; Camillo Balerna; Mauro Salazar; Alberto Cerofolini; Christopher H. Onder
Applied Energy, 282, Article 115980
High — gear/energy interactions

Combines convex powertrain modelling, dynamic programming and Pontryagin’s minimum principle to jointly optimize gearshift and energy management for minimum lap time; includes a Bahrain circuit case study.
Optimizes a modeled car with fuel/battery targets; it does not estimate hidden battery state from noisy, public-facing telemetry. Results depend on the modeled powertrain and chosen targets.
Engineer telemetry features jointly (RPM, gear, speed, throttle, braking, distance/track position) rather than independently. Use its coupled dynamics as a benchmark for feature design.
Time-optimal Energy Management of the Formula 1 Power Unit with Active Battery Path Constraints
Pol Duhr; Maximilian Schaller; Luca Arzilli; Alberto Cerofolini; Christopher Harald Onder
2021 European Control Conference (ECC), pp. 913–920
29 Jun–2 Jul 2021 (conference)
Very high — direct F1 battery constraint relevance

Studies how active upper/lower battery state-of-charge constraints change time-optimal F1 energy management, using a convex powertrain model, Pontryagin-based analysis and numerical optimization; discusses an overtake controller.

Model-based optimal-control analysis rather than inference from external telemetry; based on a prior regulation era, so numerical limits should not be carried into 2026 without checking the current FIA issue.

Use the qualitative constraint logic to keep inferred state trajectories physically plausible and to identify when deployment or recovery may be constrained. Recheck every numerical limit against 2026 regulations.
Energy Optimal Control for Formula One Race Car
Hassan Javed; Stephen Samuel
SAE Powertrains, Fuels & Lubricants Conference & Exhibition, SAE Technical Paper 2022-01-1043
High — F1 powertrain model and constraints

Builds a force-balanced F1 powertrain model and formulates energy-optimal control with regulated constraints; compares discrete optimization/genetic-algorithm results against dynamic programming and a high-fidelity simulator.

Simulation-focused and based on an earlier F1 power-unit ruleset. It explicitly notes that multiple control paths can achieve similar objectives, which limits unique inference from observed motion alone.
Use its state/constraint framing when defining a physics-informed baseline. Treat hidden ERS behaviour as an inverse problem with ambiguity, not as a uniquely recoverable value from speed alone.
Minimum-Race-Time Energy Allocation Strategies for the Hybrid-Electric Formula 1 Power Unit
Pol Duhr; Daniele Buccheri; Camillo Balerna; Alberto Cerofolini; Christopher H. Onder
IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology, 72(6), 7035–7050
Jun 2023
High — race/lap temporal coupling

Develops a nonlinear optimization framework for lap-by-lap battery and fuel consumption targets. Single-lap optimization maps are fitted with neural networks and used for race-wide energy allocation and shrinking-horizon control.

Uses an internal powertrain model and explicit fuel/battery energy targets that are not available in the public telemetry stream. The paper addresses race-level optimization, not direct state estimation.
Preserve lap/session history and estimate trajectories across time. Test whether race-phase context improves inferred deployment/recovery regimes over a sample-by-sample baseline.
State-of-Charge Estimation of Lithium-ion Battery Based on a Combined Method of Neural Network and Unscented Kalman Filter
Seyedmehdi Hosseininasab; Zhiwen Wan; Tim Bender; Giovanni Vagnoni; Lennart Bauer
2020 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
18 Nov–16 Dec 2020 (conference)
High for methods; indirect domain match

Combines an offline-trained neural-network battery model with an unscented Kalman filter. Evaluates against equivalent-circuit EKF/UKF baselines and tests initial-state offset, capacity error and current-sensor drift using WLTP laboratory data.
Requires battery-specific model inputs and real battery measurements (including current-related information) that are not documented in the public F1 telemetry schema used by this project.

Borrow the sequential ML-plus-filter architecture as a design pattern only if a defensible observation/state model can be built. Otherwise adapt the uncertainty-handling principle, not the battery model unchanged.
A Robust Extended Kalman Filtering Approach for State of Charge Estimation in Batteries
Prarthana Pillai; Krishna Rao Pattipati; Balakumar Balasingam
IEEE Journal of Emerging and Selected Topics in Industrial Electronics, 5(3), 1154–1170
Published online 5 Dec 2023; journal issue Jul 2024
High — uncertainty and model-mismatch treatment
Proposes a robust EKF that adds states to absorb battery-model parameter uncertainty and uses filter innovations to detect model-order uncertainty; demonstrated with a battery simulator.
Demonstration is based on a battery simulator and battery state-space model, not F1 telemetry. It does not solve the absence of direct electrical measurements.
Motivates sensitivity analysis, residual/innovation monitoring and uncertainty reporting. Avoid presenting inferred SoC as ground truth when the underlying model is only approximate.
State-of-Health and State-of-Charge Estimation in Electric Vehicles Batteries: A Survey on Machine Learning Approaches
Aya Haraz; Khalid Abualsaud; Ahmed Massoud
High — methods survey
Surveys machine-learning methods for battery SoC and SoH estimation, including model families, battery types, inputs, datasets, metrics and evaluation choices.
A survey of EV battery estimation, not motorsport energy inference. Its methods often assume battery measurements and ground-truth labels unavailable in the project's telemetry.
Use it to organize the ML-method comparison and evaluation section. Explicitly document the domain shift between EV battery datasets and F1 vehicle telemetry.
Data-driven state-of-charge estimation of a lithium-ion battery pack in electric vehicles based on real-world driving data
Changcheng Sun; Mingyu Gao; Hui Cai; Fei Xu; Chunxiang Zhu
Journal of Energy Storage, 101, Part B, Article 113986
High for sequence modelling; indirect domain match

Proposes a CNN–BiLSTM–Attention model for battery-pack SoC estimation from real-world EV operating data, using multivariate sequences including speed, battery voltage, current and temperature, plus cell-voltage inconsistency features.
Relies on direct battery electrical/thermal signals and labels not documented in the public F1 telemetry schema. The architecture's performance cannot be assumed to transfer across domains.
Use as a sequence-model reference and compare temporal models only with careful validation. Consider observable vehicle-dynamics features, but do not claim equivalence to voltage/current inputs.

Student-journal venue and a method that projects 2026 constraints onto 2024 sessions. The numerical assumptions and arithmetic should be independently reproduced; do not treat its reported circuit values as authoritative without checking.

Thermodynamic evaluation of 2026 Power Unit technical regulation changes in Formula 1
Jiashu Xu
Applied and Computational Engineering, 26, 145–150
Medium — background on regulation/thermodynamics
Reviews the 2023 and draft 2026 F1 power-unit rules and discusses possible thermodynamic and cost implications, including the change in electric power and removal of MGU-H.

Uses pre-final/draft regulation context and makes thermodynamic assumptions that are not all demonstrated through detailed engine data. It is not a telemetry-based estimation method; numerical rules may be outdated.
Use for historical context only. Compare every regulation-related number with the current FIA issue and avoid treating the paper's thermodynamic projections as measured 2026 performance.
